ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is a rectangular garden, with the bottom side labeled 20 m, and the height on the right side labeled 16 m. The garden is divided into three parts: left, middle, and right: the middle is a relatively narrow vertical region, and the two sides are relatively wide regions. There are six gray flower beds in total: on the left and right sides there are several horizontally placed gray rectangles, and in the middle there are two vertically placed gray rectangles, stacked one above the other. All gray flower beds have the same shape and size, only some have been rotated in direction. Reasoning: Let the short side of each flower bed be s, and the long side be l. The height 16 m in the figure is divided into 4 horizontal bands of equal height, and the height of each horizontal band is exactly the short side of a horizontally placed flower bed, so s = 16 ÷ 4 = 4. Looking along the width of 20 m, the width is composed of the long side l of one horizontally placed flower bed on the left side, the short side s of the vertically placed flower bed in the middle, and the long side l of one horizontally placed flower bed on the right side, so 2l + s = 20. Substituting s = 4, we get 2l + 4 = 20, 2l = 16, l = 8. The perimeter of each flower bed is 2(l + s) = 2(8 + 4) = 24.
